title.value: Structure Learning for Neural Module Networks
title.justification: The title is explicitly stated at the beginning of the document.
title.quote: Structure Learning for Neural Module Networks

analysis.description: The paper presents an approach to learn the module structure of Neural Module Networks (NMNs), expanding beyond learning only module parameters and execution order. It introduces Learnable Neural Module Networks (LNMNs), with results showing that learning both internal module structure and sequencing can be achieved without extra supervisory signals, performing comparably to models with hand-designed modules.

type.justification: The paper contains empirical results comparing their proposed model against other models in terms of performance on datasets like CLEVR and VQA.
type.quote: Our results show that one is indeed able to simultaneously learn both internal module structure and module sequencing without extra supervisory signals for module execution sequencing.

name.justification: The paper focuses on improving the structure learning of neural module networks for visual question answering tasks.
name.quote: Neural Module Networks, originally proposed for the task of visual question answering, are a class of neural network architectures that involve human-specified neural modules, each designed for a specific form of reasoning.

name.justification: The focus on reasoning tasks like visual question answering involves visual reasoning processes.
name.quote: Designing general purpose reasoning modules is one of the central challenges in artificial intelligence.

name.justification: This model is introduced and evaluated in the paper as a contribution.
name.quote: Our proposed model, Learnable Neural Module Network (LNMN), learns the structure of the module, the parameters of the module, and the way to compose the modules based on just the regular task loss.

is_contributed.justification: The paper presents LNMN as a new model to learn module structures automatically.
